questions.question_text: What is the minimum E&O insurance coverage required per claim for Wyoming licensees?
distractors: $50,000 per claim
$250,000 per claim
$500,000 per claim
questions.explanation: WREC Rules & Regulations Chapter 7 set the minimum errors and omissions coverage at $100,000 single-limit liability per occurrence or claim made (§ 4(a) — not including costs for investigation or defense) with a $500,000 annual aggregate (§ 4(b)). Section 8(a)(iii)(D) applies the same $100,000 / $500,000 floor to individually obtained 'equivalent' coverage. The mandate itself comes from W.S. 33-28-401, effective January 1, 2008, but the statute sets no dollar limits — subsection (c) directs the Commission to fix the minimum limits, deductible, and exemptions by rule.

questions.question_text: A licensee renews her license but fails to submit proof of E&O insurance. What action can WREC take?
questions.correct_answer: Place the license on inactive status
distractors: Issue a 90-day provisional renewal
Impose a late fee but approve renewal
Refer the matter to law enforcement
questions.explanation: WREC Rules Ch. 7 § 8(c) provides that an active licensee who fails to provide proof of coverage 'shall be placed on inactive status ... Immediately, if certification of current insurance coverage is not provided to the Commission.' Section 10 then requires the licensee to surrender the license, and § 12 bars any licensed activity until proof is filed and the license is reactivated. Failing to obtain and maintain E&O insurance is also a stand-alone ground for discipline under Ch. 6 § 1(a)(xvii), which can carry a fine, censure, probation, suspension, or revocation — but inactive status is the automatic administrative consequence.

questions.question_text: What is the maximum deductible allowed on a Wyoming licensee's E&O policy?
questions.explanation: WREC Rules Ch. 7 § 4(c) permits 'a deductible amount for each occurrence of not more than one thousand dollars for single-limit liability coverage and one thousand dollars maximum additional deductible for defense and investigation.' So the damage deductible is capped at $1,000, with a separate $1,000 maximum applying to defense and investigation costs. The cap is set by Commission rule; W.S. 33-28-401 itself contains no coverage or deductible figures.

questions.question_text: A broker activates a license that has been on inactive status for two years. When must E&O insurance proof be provided?
distractors: Within 60 days of the first transaction
At the next annual renewal date
Only if WREC requests verification
questions.explanation: Wyoming requires proof of E&O insurance when obtaining, renewing, or activating a license. Reactivating a dormant license triggers the same insurance verification requirement. The licensee cannot practice until valid coverage is confirmed.

questions.question_text: A salesperson allows her E&O policy to lapse mid-year but continues showing properties and writing offers. What is her regulatory exposure?
questions.correct_answer: Her license goes to inactive status as of the date coverage terminated
distractors: No risk until the next renewal cycle
A fine only if a claim is filed
Nothing, so long as she reinstates coverage before her renewal date
questions.explanation: WREC Rules Ch. 7 § 9 provides that when a licensee's insurer or the group plan notifies the Commission of nonpayment, 'the Commission shall place that license on inactive status as of the date of termination of coverage'; § 8(c)(ii) applies the same automatic result to lapsed equivalent coverage. Section 10 then requires her to surrender the license, and § 12 bars any licensed activity until proof of insurance is filed and the license is reactivated — so every showing and offer written after the lapse is unlicensed activity. Failing to obtain and maintain E&O is separately a ground for discipline (administrative fine, censure, probation, suspension, or revocation) under WREC Rules Ch. 6 § 1(a)(xvii) and W.S. 33-28-111(a), exposing both her and her responsible broker.

questions.question_text: What entity contracts with an insurer to provide the Wyoming group E&O program?
distractors: The Wyoming Association of Realtors
The state Department of Insurance
Each individual brokerage
questions.explanation: WREC contracts directly with an insurance provider to offer a group E&O insurance program for licensees. This state-administered program ensures affordable, accessible coverage that meets the statutory minimum requirements.

questions.question_text: A licensee finds an individual E&O policy for $200 per year with $75,000 per claim coverage. Can she use this instead of the WREC group program?
questions.correct_answer: No, it does not meet the $100,000 minimum
distractors: Yes, any E&O policy satisfies the law
Yes, if the premium is lower than the group rate
No, individual policies are never permitted
questions.explanation: Licensees may obtain individual 'equivalent' coverage instead of the WREC group program — W.S. 33-28-401(b) permits it 'if the coverage complies with the minimum requirements established by the commission.' WREC Rules Ch. 7 § 8(a)(iii)(D) sets that floor at 'not less than $100,000 for each licensed individual and entity per covered claim ... with an annual aggregate limit of not less than $500,000.' A $75,000 per-claim policy falls short, and a lower premium is irrelevant to whether the policy qualifies.

questions.question_text: A licensee prefers to get their own E&O policy rather than use the WREC group program. What must the individual policy meet?
distractors: Any coverage amount the licensee chooses
Double the group program coverage limits
Individual policies are not permitted
questions.explanation: Licensees may obtain individual E&O coverage instead of the WREC group program, but the policy must meet WREC's minimum requirements ($100,000 per claim / $500,000 aggregate with a deductible not exceeding $1,000). The group program is an option, not a mandate.

questions.question_text: A new licensee wants to opt out of the WREC group program entirely and go uninsured. Is this permitted?
questions.correct_answer: No, all active licensees must carry E&O
distractors: Yes, the group program is optional
Yes, for the first year of licensure
No, but only brokers must be insured
questions.explanation: E&O insurance is mandatory for all active Wyoming licensees, not just brokers — W.S. 33-28-401(a) states that 'All licensees shall obtain and maintain errors and omissions insurance coverage under the group program or individual coverage.' Participation in the WREC group program is optional; a licensee may instead file certification of qualifying equivalent coverage under WREC Rules Ch. 7 §§ 7-8. Carrying no coverage at all is not an option: the license is placed on inactive status (Ch. 7 §§ 8(c), 9) and the licensee may not practice until proof is filed and the license is reactivated (§ 12), and the failure is separately a ground for discipline under Ch. 6 § 1(a)(xvii).

questions.question_text: A broker obtains an individual E&O policy with $100,000 per claim and $500,000 aggregate but a $2,500 deductible. Does this meet WREC standards?
distractors: Yes, coverage amounts are sufficient
Yes, deductibles are not regulated
No, aggregate must be $1,000,000
questions.explanation: The per-claim and aggregate limits meet the WREC minimums, but the deductible does not. WREC Rules Ch. 7 § 4(c) caps the deductible at $1,000 per occurrence, plus a separate $1,000 maximum for defense and investigation, and the Commission's Errors and Omissions Insurance Certificate of Coverage — the form a privately insured licensee must file — states the requirement on its face: 'Each Claim ($100,000 minimum) ... Aggregate ($500,000 minimum) ... Deductible ($1,000 maximum).' All three requirements must be satisfied. Note the cap comes from Commission rule and the certification form, not from W.S. 33-28-401, which sets no coverage dollar figures.
